headline: Toxic Plume Chokes The Narrows After AP-9 Stack Failure
body:
A catastrophic failure in Atmospheric Processor Unit AP-9, operated under a Palladian municipal contract, released an estimated 40,000 cubic meters of sulfuric particulate and unfiltered industrial offgas over The Narrows at approximately 0340 hours this morning. The cloud, visible as a pale yellow haze from as far as The Circuit, settled at street level within ninety minutes, forcing residents into sealed rooms or onto rooftops. Emergency venting protocols — required under the 2129 Clean Air Compact — were never activated. Palladian has not responded to requests for comment.

By dawn, Meridian Emergency Services logged over 1,200 respiratory distress calls from the district. Sector clinics operating under Helix Biosystems contracts were overwhelmed within two hours, with triage overflow spilling onto Conduit Row and the upper decks of the Narrows Stack Towers. 'My daughter's BCI started throwing oxygen-low alerts at 0400 and I had no way to get her out,' said Rafi Osei-Volkov, a resident of Level 7, Block 22. 'There were no evacuation notices. Nothing.'

Palladian released a brief statement at 0900 attributing the failure to 'an unforeseeable cascade event in tertiary filtration' and promising a full review. Critics immediately pointed to a 2134 Lake Monitor investigation that documented 14 deferred maintenance requests on AP-9, all denied on cost grounds. The Federal Remnant's Environmental Oversight Division has opened a preliminary inquiry, though enforcement powers in Palladian-contracted zones remain legally disputed.

The Narrows Air Quality Index remains at 340 — classified as Hazardous — as of this broadcast. Residents without sealed housing or functioning BCI environmental filters are advised to shelter in place. Community organizers from The Collective have established three makeshift filter stations on Level 4, running on diverted power from the maintenance grid.
aftermath: Palladian settled a class-action claim eighteen months later for 4.2 million phi — approximately 3,500 phi per affected household — while admitting no wrongdoing, and AP-9 remained offline for six months pending repairs that residents say were never fully completed.
casualties: 23 confirmed dead, 1,400+ treated for respiratory injury
runner_relevance: The AP-9 failure created immediate demand for smuggling and courier contracts — residents and underground clinics needed emergency medical supplies (sealed respirators, BCI oxygen-mod patches, Helix-brand bronchodilators) moved into The Narrows fast, bypassing the Palladian logistics blockade on relief shipments. Longer-term, The Collective and several anonymous clients posted data-retrieval contracts seeking the suppressed Palladian maintenance logs as litigation evidence, and at least three extraction contracts surfaced to pull high-value targets — a Palladian mid-level engineer rumored to be willing to testify — out of corporate housing before they could be silenced.
